authorship_conflict: Auditor authored train-a and dev/test scenarios. This audit is not an independent gold-quality review; separate agent semantic reviews remain required.
methods: Read-only replay of all current families and prior faults, with exact equality to all six on-disk record/SFT files.
Exact source-prefix matching, arrived-evidence checks, previous-state cursor/history checks, strict metadata-key and neutral patch-ID checks on all 650 model inputs.

Cross-split exact full-dialogue, normalized user-dialogue, normalized prefix and complete model-input collision checks. NFKC/lowercase, speaker-name replacement and numeric masking normalize names/numbers.

TF-IDF cosine over English words/bigrams and Chinese character bigrams; three nearest foreign-split families per held-out family, 90 directed candidates, individually model-reviewed from raw dialogues.
Five additional thematic/cross-language comparisons, including sewing and email workflows that lexical overlap misses.

thematic_candidates.model_semantic_review: Both involve sewing, but a sleeve-length correction with removable fitting stitches and cancelled explanation differs from a reversible tote, seam allowance, closure replacement and pocket cancellation. Domain-disjoint claims would be false.

Both are email classification workflows with a label rename and no deletion. Dev additionally revises tags-only to allow stars and distinguishes an archive explanation from adoption; train has TEST-subject exception, a second shipment rule and display-priority question. These are not mere name/number substitutions, but transfer is within a shared workflow.
Both are observation templates; weather diary missing-value handling and restored cloud sketches differ from compost odor conditions and withdrawn photo IDs. Measurement-log construction is shared.

Phenology observations and bird observations share natural-history logging; bloom condition/tree expansion/no interventions differ from withdrawing location while keeping date and precise-coordinate exclusion.

Browser grouping and mail triage are digital-organization tasks but differ in pinned exclusions/fallback groups versus subject conditions/star actions. Both resist assistant destructive-action suggestions.

conclusion: No exact reuse or detected future/gold/scaffolding leakage in the pinned 650 exports. Reviewed candidates are different scenarios, but several share domains, workflows, operation patterns and synthetic authoring style. Treat results as family-held-out synthetic transfer, not domain-disjoint or real-user performance.
limitations: Lexical similarity is weak across languages and cannot rule out every semantic paraphrase; the thematic review is bounded rather than exhaustive cross-language embedding analysis.
Both train and held-out data intentionally share intention-update mechanisms and several domains; arbitrary top-three selection is a diagnostic shortlist, not a proof of independence.
All five prefixes from a family are correlated; 650 rows represent 130 scenario families.
This checks export contents, not actual trainer completion-loss masks, token truncation, checkpoint selection, or whether a training process later accesses test data.
Exact comparison with the earlier 24 exposed examples excludes literal normalized-prefix reuse, not all possible shared mechanisms or semantic motifs.
